a: Name of the package(s) to be installed. Set to all to run the action on all the installed packages.
Allow empty checksums to be used for downloaded resource from non-secure locations. Use chocolatey.chocolatey.win_chocolatey_feature with the name allowEmptyChecksums to control this option globally.

This option is deprecated and will be removed in v2.0.0 of this collection. Chocolatey CLI has deprecated side-by-side installations as of its v1.2.0 release and plans to remove them in its v2.0.0 release.
Allow the installation of pre-release packages. If state is latest, the latest pre-release package will be installed.
Force Chocolatey to install the package of a specific process architecture. When setting x86, will ensure Chocolatey installs the x86 package even when on an x64 bit OS.

Specify the bootstrap script URL that can be used to install Chocolatey if it is not already present on the system. Use this parameter when name is chocolatey to ensure that a custom bootstrap script is used.
Specify the TLS versions used when retrieving and invoking the bootstrap_script to install Chocolatey if it is not already installed on the system.
Override a package's checksums for files downloaded during installation. If the checksum is not MD5, you will need to specify the checksum_type as well.
Override a package's checksums for 64-bit files downloaded during installation. If the checksum is not MD5, you will need to specify the checksum_type64 as well.
Override a package's checksum type for files downloaded during install. Use in conjunction with checksum.
Override a package's checksum type for files downloaded during install. Use in conjunction with checksum64.
Additional parameters to pass to choco.exe These may be any additional parameters to pass through directly to Chocolatey, in addition to the arguments already specified via other parameters.
Forces the install of a package, even if it already is installed. Using force will cause Ansible to always report that a change was made.
Ignore the checksums provided by the package. Use chocolatey.chocolatey.win_chocolatey_feature with the name checksumFiles to control this option globally.
Ignore dependencies, only install/upgrade the package itself.
Ignores any pins and upgrades the package(s) anyway. Chocolatey CLI (choco) v2.3.0 and higher is required to use this option.

These are arguments that are passed directly to the installer run by the Chocolatey package, for example MSI properties or command-line arguments for the specific native installer used by the package.
Override arguments of native installer with arguments provided by user. Should install arguments be used exclusively without appending to current package passed arguments.
Parameters to pass to the package's chocolateyInstall script. These are parameters specific to the Chocolatey package and are generally documented by the package itself.
Whether to pin the Chocolatey package or not. If omitted then no checks on package pins are done. Will pin/unpin the specific version if version is set.

Proxy password used to install Chocolatey and the package. This value is exposed as a command argument and any privileged account can see this value when the module is running Chocolatey, define the password on the…
Proxy URL used to install chocolatey and the package. Use chocolatey.chocolatey.win_chocolatey_config with the name proxy to control this option globally.
Proxy username used to install Chocolatey and the package. Before Ansible 2.7, users with double quote characters " would need to be escaped with \ beforehand. This is no longer necessary.
Remove a package's dependencies on uninstall.
Do not run chocolateyInstall.ps1 or chocolateyUninstall.ps1 scripts when installing a package.
Specify the source to retrieve the package from. Use chocolatey.chocolatey.win_chocolatey_source to manage global sources.

The password for source_username. This value is exposed as a command argument and any privileged account can see this value when the module is running Chocolatey, define the credentials with a source with…

A username to use with source when accessing a feed that requires authentication. It is recommended you define the credentials on a source with chocolatey.chocolatey.win_chocolatey_source instead of passing it per task.
State of the package on the system. When absent, will ensure the package is not installed. When present, will ensure the package is installed.
The time (in seconds) to allow chocolatey to finish before timing out.

Used when downloading the Chocolatey install script if Chocolatey is not already installed, this does not affect the Chocolatey package install process. When no, no SSL certificates will be validated.
Specific version of the package to be installed. When state is set to absent, will uninstall the specific version otherwise all versions of that package will be removed.
The name of the config setting to manage. See https://chocolatey.org/docs/chocolatey-configuration for a list of valid configuration settings that can be changed.
When absent, it will ensure the setting is unset or blank. When present, it will ensure the setting is set to the value of value.
Used when state that contains the value to set for the config setting. Cannot be null or an empty string, use state to unset a config value instead.
If supplied, restrict the facts collected to the given subset. Possible values: all, config, feature, outdated, packages, sources. You can provide a list of values to specify a larger subset.
chocolatey.chocolatey.win_chocolatey_fac.d: Create a facts collection for Chocolatey

a: The name of the feature to manage. Run choco.exe feature list to get a list of features that can be managed. For a list of options see Chocolatey feature docs
When disabled then the feature will be disabled. When enabled then the feature will be enabled.
The name of the source to configure.
Makes the source visible to Administrators only. Requires Chocolatey >= 0.10.8. When creating a new source, this defaults to false.
Allow the source to be used with self-service Requires Chocolatey >= 0.10.4. When creating a new source, this defaults to false.
Bypass the proxy when using this source. Requires Chocolatey >= 0.10.4. When creating a new source, this defaults to false.
The path to a .pfx file to use for X509 authenticated feeds. Requires Chocolatey >= 0.9.10.
The password for certificate if required. Requires Chocolatey >= 0.9.10.
The priority order of this source compared to other sources, lower is better. All priorities above 0 will be evaluated first, then zero-based values will be evaluated in config file order.
The file/folder/url of the source. Required when state is present or disabled and the source does not already exist.
The password for source_username. Required if source_username is set.
The username used to access source.
When absent, will remove the source. When disabled, will ensure the source exists but is disabled. When present, will ensure the source exists and is enabled.

When always, the module will always set the password and report a change if certificate_password or source_password is set. When on_create, the module will only set the password if the source is being created.
